Rules / Tests

SK8007 Use controlled assertion input

An xUnit assertion directly consumes a live clock, a new GUID or an unseeded random value.

CategoryTests
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since1.3

Why

Live environmental input makes an assertion harder to reproduce. Prefer a controlled clock, a fixed identifier or an explicitly seeded random source where the test permits it. Real-clock and randomness-contract tests can be intentional, so the diagnostic requests review rather than inventing test data.

Example

Instead of:

[Fact] public void Check() { Assert.Equal(expected, DateTime.UtcNow); }

Write:

[Fact] public void Check() { Assert.Equal(expected, controlledClock.GetUtcNow()); }

When it does not fire

Initial coverage is xUnit: recognized Assert calls directly in semantically attributed Fact/Theory methods (including derived attributes). Framework DateTime.Now/UtcNow/Today, DateTimeOffset.Now/UtcNow, Guid.NewGuid, and Random.Shared or new Random() calls to Next/NextInt64/NextDouble/NextSingle are recognized. Seeded or unknown random instances, custom clocks/assertions, diagnostic-message arguments, nameof operands, deferred lambdas, local functions, helpers, variables carrying earlier nondeterministic values and other test frameworks are excluded. At most one finding is emitted per assertion. Deliberate clock/randomness tests may require scoped suppression. No automatic fix is offered.

Configuration

  • dotnet_diagnostic.SK8007.severity
